headline: Dengue NS1 test made free at public hospitals until Dec 31
summary: The government has waived the fee for early diagnosis tests to encourage early detection amid an ongoing outbreak.
details: The government has made the dengue NS1 test free at all public hospitals until December 31 this year. This move aims to encourage early diagnosis as the country faces an ongoing outbreak.
The Health Services Division has instructed the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) to ensure the test is provided free of charge at government facilities through the end of the year.
The NS1 test, which is used to detect dengue infection in its early stages, previously cost Tk 50 at government hospitals. It has been offered for free during previous periods of high transmission.
For private hospitals, the government has fixed the maximum charge for the NS1 test at Tk 300.
Abu Hussain Md Moinul Ahsan, director (hospitals and clinics) at the DGHS, stated that the decision was made to encourage people to get tested early as cases surge.
June saw a sharp rise in infections and fatalities, accounting for 48 percent of all reported cases and 72 percent of deaths recorded so far this year.
Health experts warn that infections and fatalities could increase further in July and August, the peak monsoon months, unless efforts to control Aedes mosquitoes are intensified.

headline_marked: BNP leader's [[body exhumed 5 months after death]] for murder probe
headline: BNP leader's body exhumed 5 months after death for murder probe
summary: The body of Mohammad Mohibuzzaman Kochi was dug up from Tutpara Graveyard to determine the exact cause of death following a court order.
details: The body of former Khulna city BNP office secretary Mohammad Mohibuzzaman Kochi was exhumed today, nearly five months after his death.
The exhumation follows a court order for a fresh autopsy to determine the exact cause of death as part of a murder investigation by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI).
Kochi, 63, died on February 12 while serving as a polling agent for BNP candidate Nazrul Islam Monju at the Khulna Alia Kamil Madrasa polling centre during the national parliamentary election.
According to the case statement, Kochi was allegedly assaulted inside the polling centre after protesting against voter intimidation and attempts to influence votes.
The complaint alleges that the then acting principal of the madrasa, Md Abdur Rahim Sardar, grabbed him by the throat and pushed him, causing him to hit a tree.
He was later declared dead at Khulna City Medical College Hospital, sparking controversy over whether he died from the assault or a heart attack.
Former Khulna Sadar Thana BNP organising secretary Md Yusuf Harun Majnu filed a murder case, naming three accused and 15 to 20 unidentified individuals.
The body was exhumed from Tutpara Graveyard around noon in the presence of an Executive Magistrate and sent for a second post-mortem examination.
caption:
A body exhumed 5 months later. A murder probe into a polling center assault.

The body of former Khulna city BNP office secretary Mohammad Mohibuzzaman Kochi was exhumed today, nearly five months after his death.

The exhumation follows a court order for a fresh autopsy to determine the exact cause of death as part of a murder investigation by the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI).

Kochi, 63, died on February 12 while serving as a polling agent for BNP candidate Nazrul Islam Monju at the Khulna Alia Kamil Madrasa polling centre during the national parliamentary election.

According to the case statement, Kochi was allegedly assaulted inside the polling centre after protesting against voter intimidation and attempts to influence votes.

The complaint alleges that the then acting principal of the madrasa, Md Abdur Rahim Sardar, grabbed him by the throat and pushed him, causing him to hit a tree.

He was later declared dead at Khulna City Medical College Hospital, sparking controversy over whether he died from the assault or a heart attack.

Former Khulna Sadar Thana BNP organising secretary Md Yusuf Harun Majnu filed a murder case, naming three accused and 15 to 20 unidentified individuals.

The body was exhumed from Tutpara Graveyard around noon in the presence of an Executive Magistrate and sent for a second post-mortem examination.
